transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-28
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Nina Roberts (Ledgerly CTO), Carlos Mendes (Lead Backend), Aisha Khan (PM)

Auto-summary: quick sync on SDK integration and structured output parsing, reviewed recent test results, agreed on next steps for dedicated latency run and security questionnaire.

Transcript:
[00:00:03] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. quick roll call?
[00:00:08] Nina: Nina here.
[00:00:10] Carlos: Carlos on the line.
[00:00:12] Aisha: Aisha here.
[00:00:15] Jordan: Great. Priya from our eng team is joining to go over the SDK patch and the tool calling flow. Priya, want to intro?
[00:00:22] Priya: Yep hi all, Priya Patel, I'm the SE working with Ledgerly on the app integration. Today I want to cover three things: quick run through of the SDK change, how we're handling tool/function calls and the structured output schema updates, and then look at the latest benchmark numbers you ran in sandbox.
[00:00:38] Carlos: Sounds good. we did another run yesterday, same dataset as before, lots of prompts from payments flows.
[00:00:45] Jordan: Perfect, let's start SDK. Priya, what changed?
[00:00:48] Priya: The main change is we added a retry/backoff handler in the client SDK for transient errors during tool calls. We also added a helper to parse function-call style structured output into your internal event schema. There is an example in the patch — note, the auto-transcribe might show Redwood Dedi-cate in some docs but it's Redwood Dedicated.
[00:01:08] Carlos: Nice, were there any breaking changes?
[00:01:10] Priya: No breaking changes. It's opt-in. You can turn on the structured parser or use your existing JSON parsing. The parser tolerates common ASR-ish issues — sometimes the model returns slightly different key names so we added fuzzy key mapping.
[00:01:26] Aisha: That fuzzy mapping will help — our product QA found a few missing fields last week.
[00:01:31] Nina: On the security side we need to know KMS details and SSO metadata before we run anything in Prod. also SOC2 scope questions.
[00:01:40] Jordan: Understood. We'll attach the SOC2 cert and the KMS/HSM integration notes in the follow-up. Priya, quick note on telemetry?
[00:01:48] Priya: We emit request-level traces and token-cost breakdowns. For private deployments we can integrate with your SIEM, and we maintain audit logs with per-request headers. Sometimes the transcript will show KV cache as K V cash — that's just a transcription artifact — but rest assured the runtime supports prefix/KV cache and it's configurable.
[00:02:06] Carlos: Good. On yesterday's run, numbers were: hosted API avg latency 90ms, p95 160ms, p99 ~420ms. On a small Dedicated pool we saw avg 60ms, p95 95ms, p99 140ms. The cost delta looked reasonable but we need more runs to be confident.
[00:02:28] Priya: Thanks for those numbers — that matches what we expected given batch sizes. We suspect the p99 skew on hosted is due to occasional cold-starts and multi-tenant queuing. Dedicated avoids that. Also our KV cache warmup helps once you hit steady-state.
[00:02:44] Aisha: what's our target? Nina, do you have SLA expectations?
[00:02:48] Nina: For user-facing payments flows we want p95 < 150ms and p99 < 300ms if possible. We're flexible in the POC but that's the goal.
[00:02:58] Jordan: Ok good target. For the POC we can focus on optimizing batch sizes and cache TTLs. Priya, can you remind them of the batching knobs in the SDK?
[00:03:06] Priya: Sure. You can configure max_batch_latency_ms, max_batch_size, and enable continuous-batching. There's also a per-route override so you can have stricter latency on critical routes and higher throughput on background routes.
[00:03:18] Carlos: We tried max_batch_size 8 and latency 20ms — it hit the throughput we needed but p99 was a bit worse on hosted.
[00:03:25] Priya: Right, so on hosted you'll trade a bit of p99 for throughput. On Dedicated, you can bump batch size to 16 or 32 safely. Also try enabling the KV cache for payment-step prompts; that reduced token usage in our internal tests.
[00:03:40] Aisha: About structured output — our schema requires an events array, each event has type, timestamp, amount_cents, and metadata map. The last few outputs we got had amount as a string instead of int. Is that the model or our parser?
[00:03:54] Priya: It's a mix. Sometimes the model emits strings; the parser will coerce types when possible. We added schema validators in the SDK so you can fail-fast and surface examples to the evals dashboard. We'll include a sample of the coercion behavior in the patch.
[00:04:10] Carlos: Any known issues with tool/function calling? We saw a few duplicated external api calls in the logs.
[00:04:15] Priya: Duplications usually come from retries without idempotency keys. The SDK now attaches a request-id and the recommended pattern is to pass idempotency_key from your side into the tool call meta. We'll add a snippet to the docs.
[00:04:28] Nina: On data residency — the pilot data stays in sandbox, but for Prod we need EU residency for EU customers. Does Redwood offer region pinning?
[00:04:36] Jordan: Yes we do. Hosted can be pinned to a region for data residency; Dedicated gives you full control. For Private deployments we can do VPC-only. We'll include region options in the cost sheet.
[00:04:48] Aisha: Quick question: the structured output examples in the docs were a bit trimmed — can you include a full example with nested metadata?
[00:04:55] Priya: Absolutely. The patch will contain a full example including nested metadata and how to flatten or keep nested fields depending on your serialization choices.
[00:05:04] Carlos: Great. One more on cost — can you send a cost comparison for the traffic profile we shared? We want to see per-1000-request pricing and token cost under quantized models.
[00:05:12] Jordan: Yes. I'll send a per-1k and per-10k breakdown, including recommended quantization and batching profiles for Ledgerly's workload.
[00:05:20] Nina: Also, we need to confirm encryption in transit and at rest, plus whether Redwood stores raw requests in logs.
[00:05:26] Priya: Encryption at rest and in transit is standard. For hosted logs we retain request metadata and aggregated tokens; raw request bodies can be disabled or redacted. For Dedicated/Private, you control retention. We'll attach the log retention options.
[00:05:40] Jordan: Alright let's run through the runbook for next week: Priya will push the SDK patch, Jordan will send benchmark sheet, Ledgerly runs the Dedicated 1k test, Nina returns security contact info. Anything else?
[00:05:52] Aisha: Can we also do a quick smoke test with SSO — just to confirm the metadata mapping?
[00:05:56] Jordan: Yes, we'll schedule SSO smoke during the dedicated demo. Target week of Nov 9.
[00:06:02] Carlos: I'll coordinate the run and upload logs. Expect some noisy outliers — our test harness sometimes hits an intermittent networking spike.
[00:06:09] Priya: Noted. When you upload logs please include full request IDs so we can correlate. Also include the SDK version.
[00:06:17] Carlos: Will do.
[00:06:20] Nina: About compliance: is there a way to get more detailed KMS diagrams? Our security team will want the HSM flow.
[00:06:28] Priya: Yes we'll attach an architecture diagram and HSM keyflow doc. It's in the security bundle we'll send.
[00:06:35] Jordan: Any competitors in the running we should be aware of?
[00:06:38] Nina: We're also looking at OpenAI hosted endpoints and one vendor called ModelHostX for self-hosted. Anthropic was briefly evaluated but not a fit for structured outputs.
[00:06:48] Jordan: Good to know. We'll make sure our cost and latency comparisons highlight where Dedicated helps.
[00:06:54] Aisha: timeline check — we want to decide vendor by end of Nov. Does that align?
[00:06:59] Nina: Yes, end of November for decision. We have internal budget reviews mid-November.
[00:07:05] Jordan: Ok, we'll prioritize getting the SDK and benchmarks to you this week. Anything else from Ledgerly?
[00:07:12] Carlos: No, that's it.
[00:07:14] Aisha: Nope.
[00:07:16] Priya: One more small note — for retries the SDK will expose a toggle for at-least-once vs at-most-once semantics; default is at-least-once but with idempotency key it's safe to use at-most-once mode. We'll call that out in the docs.
[00:07:30] Jordan: Perfect. I'll recap after the call. Thanks everyone.
[00:07:35] Nina: Thanks.
[00:07:36] Carlos: Thanks all.

End of transcript.
